description.value: We assessed changes in cerebral blood flow (CBF) from before to after an emotional task and used these changes to predict stress, positive and negative emotional inertia in daily life events.

spans.text: In this study, we assessed changes in cerebral blood flow (CBF) from before to after an emotional task and used these changes to predict stress, positive and negative emotional inertia in daily life events.

value: We hypothesized that CBF changes in brain regions associated with emotion regulation, depression, and/or the duration of emotional experiences such as the vmPFC, dmPFC/daCC, lPFC, striatum and amygdala would be associated with emotional inertia in daily life.

value: Post-task CBF in the right occipital cortex predicted increased stress inertia.
Occipital cortex CBF was associated with increased stress inertia, although its role in these elements of depression will need to be illuminated in future investigations.

value: Post-task CBF in the right lPFC predicted decreased stress inertia.
Increases in CBF in the lPFC from before to after an emotional task predicted decreases in emotional inertia during daily life.
The lPFC may feature a general inhibitory mechanism responsible for limiting the impact that the emotional states from one event have on the emotional states of a subsequent event.
